This is a Flask fork with the package renamed to `tessel`. In it, `VerbView` is the class-based view with `get()` and `post()`.

**Building the view function**
- `VerbView` subclasses `View` in `src/tessel/views.py`.
- `View.to_view_func(name, ...)` (`views.py:86`) is a classmethod that returns a plain function, `view(**kwargs)`.
- On each request, `view()` creates a new instance of the class (`init_every_request=True`) and calls `self.run_view(**kwargs)`. If `init_every_request=False`, it reuses one shared instance.
- It then sets `view.view_class`, `view.methods` and `view.provide_automatic_options`, and applies any `decorators`.

**Working out the allowed methods**
- `VerbView.__init_subclass__` (`views.py:165`) runs when you define the subclass.
- It checks each name in `http_method_funcs` (`get`, `post` and so on) and adds the upper-cased name to `cls.methods` if the class defines it. It also inherits `methods` from base classes.

**Registering the route**
- `App.attach_route_rule` (`src/tessel/sansio/app.py:606`) takes `view_func.methods` when no explicit `methods` is passed. It falls back to `("GET",)` if there are none.
- It adds `OPTIONS` if `provide_automatic_options` is set.
- It creates the `url_rule_class` rule with that method set and adds it to `url_map` (`app.py:651-654`).
- This is why the URL router only lets matching HTTP methods reach the view.

**Dispatching to get/post**
- `VerbView.run_view` (`views.py:182`) does `getattr(self, request.method.lower())`.
- A `HEAD` request falls back to `get` if there is no `head` handler.
- If there is still no handler, an assertion fails.
- It calls the handler through `active_app.ensure_sync(meth)(**kwargs)`, so async handlers work too.
